The global scope of this PKGBUILD consists of standard variable definitions (`pkgname`, `pkgver`, `source`, `depends`, `sha256sums`, etc.) and one function definition (`package() { ... }`). The file uses `'` and `"` HTML entities in place of shell quote characters, which is non‑standard and causes bash to misinterpret several lines (the `&` is parsed as a background control operator, breaking the intended assignments). Despite this malformed syntax, the globally executed commands are limited to harmless variable assignments and failing background command invocations that do not exfiltrate data, download further payloads, or establish persistence. No command substitutions (`$(...)`), backticks, `eval`, `exec`, `curl`, or `wget` are present in the top‑level scope. The `package()` function body is not executed by `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. Therefore, sourcing this PKGBUILD to extract its metadata poses no security risk.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Global scope has no malicious code execution, only broken syntax.</summary>
</security_assessment>
